content.content: # Generated JavaScript test suite Copy the suite and its config into the ported implementation, then run it: ```sh cd /workspace/ported_implementation cp -r /workspace/tests/javascript tests cp tests/vitest.config.unit.ts . npx vitest run --config vitest.config.unit.ts ``` The config aliases `gbnf` to `/workspace/ported_implementation/src/index.ts`. Repoint it if your entry file differs. // The alias is absolute because vitest rejects relative ones. export default { test: { include: [ 'tests/**/*.test.ts', ], watchExclude: [ 'tmp/**/*', ], globals: true, }, resolve: { alias: { gbnf: '/workspace/ported_implementation/src/index.ts', }, }, }; # Generated Python test suite Copy the suite into the ported implementation, then run it: ```sh cd /workspace/ported_implementation cp -r /workspace/tests/python tests uv run --offline --no-project --with pytest==9.1.1 --with pytest-describe==3.2.0 python -m pytest tests ``` Run it as written. `python -m pytest` puts the working directory on `sys.path`, so `import gbnf` resolves from the port root. Set `PYTHONPATH` if your package lives somewhere else. A `pytest` is also on `PATH`, but running it directly leaves the working directory off `sys.path`, and `pytest tests` fails to import the package under test. The bare `python` has no pytest of its own — `uv run` is what supplies it. The versions are pinned to what the image's uv cache holds. `--offline` reads only that cache, so changing either pin makes the command fail to resolve. === REF README # GBNF A library for parsing `.gbnf` grammar files in Python. ## Install ```bash pip install gbnf ``` === pyproject [project] name = "gbnf" version = "0.0.30" readme = "README.md" requires-python = ">=3.11" dependencies = [ "pytest-watcher>=0.4.3",] description = "A library for parsing GBNF grammars" classifiers = [ "Programming Language :: Python :: 3", "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License", "Operating System :: OS Independent",] [[project.authors]] name = "Ambient Labs" email = "maintainers@gbnf.dev" [build-system] requires = [ "setuptools",] build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta" [project.urls] Homepage = "https://github.com/ambient-labs/GBNF/packages/gbnf" "Bug Tracker" = "https://github.com/ambient-labs/GBNF/packages/gbnf/issues" [tool.ruff] line-length = 120 preview = true [tool.uv] dev-dependencies = [ "pytest-describe>=2.2.0", "pytest-watcher>=0.4.3", "pytest>=8.3.3",] [tool.ruff.lint] extend-select = [ "A", "ARG", "B", "BLE", "COM", "E", "F", "FA", "FIX", "FLY", "FURB", "G", "I", "ICN", "ISC", "INP", "PERF", "PGH", "PIE", "PT", "PTH", "RET", "RSE", "RUF", "SLOT", "T20", "TD", "TID", "UP", "W", "YTT",] ignore = [ "TD002", "TD003", "TID252", "FIX002", "BLE001", "FLY002",] fixable = [ "ALL",] unfixable = [] [tool.ruff.format] quote-style = "double" indent-style = "space" skip-magic-trailing-comma = false line-ending = "auto" [tool.pytest.ini_options] minversion = "6.0" testpaths = [ "gbnf/**/*_test.py",] [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores] "**/*_test.py" = [ "T201", "RUF012", "PERF203", "FLY002", "ARG001", "B008", "ARG002", "A002", "A001",] [tool.setuptools.packages.find] where = [ ".",] include = [ "gbnf*",]

The port is complete and the full suite is green: **773/773 tests passing across all 6 files.**

## What was ported

`reference_implementation/gbnf/` (Python) → `ported_implementation/src/` (TypeScript), module-for-module with kebab-case filenames and camelCase identifiers:

- **`rules-builder/`** — `RulesBuilder`, `SymbolIds`, `parseChar`/`parseName`/`parseSpace`/`isWordChar`, internal rule-def types
- **`grammar-parser/build-rule-stack.ts`** — linear rule defs → per-path rule stacks
- **`grammar-graph/`** — `Graph`, `GraphNode`, `GraphPointer`, `Pointers`, `ParseState`, `RuleRef`, type guards, serialization, printing
- **`utils/errors/`** — `GrammarParseError`, `InputParseError` (incl. `errorForMostRecentInput`/`src` getters), `buildErrorPosition`
- **`index.ts`** — default + named `GBNF`, `RuleType`, `GrammarParseError`, `InputParseError`, and the rule types

Also added `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and copied `tests/` + `vitest.config.unit.ts` per the suite README (`npx vitest run --config vitest.config.unit.ts`).

## Notable translation decisions

- **Rules are plain discriminated-union objects** (`{ type: 'char', value }`, `'char_exclude'`, `'end'`) rather than Python's dataclasses. The tests compare rules structurally against object literals, and `RuleType` is a real exported enum. `RuleRef` stays a class because its `nodes` accessor throws when unset, as in the reference.
- **Deterministic ordering.** Python stores a `RuleRef`'s target nodes in a `set` (arbitrary iteration order); JS `Set` preserves insertion order, so the port emits rules in graph order. That's what the JS suite pins, and it's the intended order — a side-by-side run against the reference shows identical rule *sets* and `size` values, differing only in that ordering.
- **Fixed the unique-rule dedup.** The Python `Graph` constructor overwrites `unique_rules[key]` on every rule, making its "always use the same reference for an identical rule" comment a no-op. The port sets it only when absent. Behaviour is unchanged (it only affects how pointers group by rule), so this is safe.
- **`Graph.print()` works here but crashes in the reference** — Python's `print.py` reads `rule.type`, which its `Rule` classes don't define, so any grammar with an end/ref node raises `AttributeError`. Since the port's rules carry `type`, printing works (verified manually; no test covers it).
- **Time limit** uses `performance.now()` with a 1000 **ms** default, vs. `perf_counter()`/1000 **seconds** in Python. Nothing in the suite exercises it; grammar parsing here is sub-millisecond.
- Dropped `validate_non_empty`, which is dead code in the reference (attached as dataclass `field` metadata, never invoked).

One caveat: `tsc` isn't installable in this sandbox (npm registry returns 403), so the types are hand-audited, not compiler-verified — vitest's esbuild transform strips types without checking them. `npm run typecheck` is wired up for when a compiler is available.
